_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Deepak Nitrite (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: Advanced Intermediates and Phenolics each grow revenue and earn an EBITDA margin (segment EBIT + segment depreciation). A third line removes inter-segment sales. Group EBITDA = sum of segments less central costs (Screener basis, excluding other income). Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates
segments._why: FY27: Q1 +33% (better prices after the Middle East war, recovery in nitrites and fuel additives, new nitration/hydrogenation output); Q2-Q4 assumed +12% as war-time prices fade, with the multipurpose agro-intermediates and alkylation plants adding volume only from January 2027. FY28 +12%: first full year of the new DCTL plants and fluorination products. FY29 +10%. AI revenue was ₹3,034 cr in FY23; we reach ₹3,700 cr only in FY29.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 26.6% (FY22), 20.8% (FY23), 19.6% (FY24), 11.4% (FY25), 9.3% (FY26). Q1FY27 EBIT margin 8.3% (~13% EBITDA). Captive nitric acid (once it runs reliably), China's curbs on nitration and new products should lift margins, but Chinese pricing still sets the ceiling: 12.5% / 14.5% / 15.5%, well below the FY22-24 levels.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments._why: FY27: Q1 ₹1,775 cr (+36%) on war-time spreads (West Asia supply disruptions); we assume ~₹1,500 cr a quarter for Q2-Q4 as prices normalise and Haldia Petrochemicals' new 345 ktpa phenol plant (due to start in October 2026) starts selling: +17%. FY28 +2%: lower phenol/acetone prices offset by ~10% more volume (debottlenecking to ~400 ktpa) and the first full year of MIBK/MIBC and acetophenone. FY29 +10%: volume growth plus a small start to polycarbonate (commissioning targeted H2 FY28-29).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 12.5% (FY20), 28.1% (FY21), 22.6% (FY22), 13.8-14.9% (FY23-26, including a Gujarat GST incentive worth ~1.9-2.8 points in FY25-26). Q1FY27 ~25% (EBIT 23.5%). We assume ~25% in Q1, ~19% in Q2 and ~12% in H2 (FY27: 17.5%), then 14% (mid-cycle, incentive included) as a new domestic competitor and Chinese capacity cap spreads.

segments.name: Inter-segment eliminations
segments._why: Sales between the segments, removed on consolidation: ₹50 cr (FY25), ₹67 cr (FY26), only ₹1 cr in Q1FY27. We assume ~₹40 cr in FY27, growing 10% a year.

_unallocLabel: Central costs not allocated to segments (reported EBITDA below the sum of segment EBITDA)
_unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA (which excludes other income): ₹34 cr (FY22), ₹24 cr (FY23), ₹58 cr (FY25), ₹39 cr (FY26); FY24 ₹128 cr includes items Screener moved to other income. We assume ₹45-55 cr as head office grows with DCTL.
_capexWhy: Guidance ~₹2,500 cr for FY27 (Feb-2026), of which ₹1,500-1,600 cr for the polycarbonate programme (Aug-2026); ~₹3,000 cr on polycarbonate in 2027-28 plus debottlenecking and maintenance; FY29 completes PC and starts BPA (₹2,500 cr approved Aug-2026). Total FY27-29 ₹8,600 cr; FY26 actual ₹1,199 cr.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹225 cr = 5.5% of average gross block. The engine depreciates all capex at once, but most of the FY27-29 spend sits in capital work in progress until polycarbonate starts (H2 FY28-29). 4.3% gives ~₹250 cr / ~₹380 cr / ~₹510 cr: slightly low for FY27 (Q1 run-rate ₹64 cr a quarter plus new plants), slightly high for FY28, and FY29 includes part-year PC depreciation.
_treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income entered separately.
_otherIncomeWhy: Other income ₹45 cr in FY26 (normal, Screener), ₹14 cr in Q1FY27; cash balances fall as capex is funded.
_interestWhy: FY26 ₹46 cr; Q1FY27 ₹23 cr. Borrowings rise to ~₹7,500 cr by FY29 (management: peak ₹8,000-8,500 cr), but interest on the PC loans is capitalised until commissioning (Ind AS 23). FY29 includes part-year interest on the PC debt after start-up.
_taxWhy: FY26 effective 27.3% (incl. CSR and other disallowances); Q1FY27 26.2%; statutory 25.17%.
_payoutWhy: ₹7.5 a share for four years (FY26 payout 19%); we assume the dividend stays near ₹7-8 while capex is heavy.

dcf._betaWhy: Commodity-linked chemicals with a large project under way: market-like risk.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian demand for phenol, acetone and polycarbonate tracks industrial growth; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth of ~12% in FY30 and 14% in FY31 as polycarbonate (165 ktpa, ~₹4,000 cr of revenue at full rates) ramps up; then 6% for ever.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: An integrated propylene-to-polycarbonate chain should earn more than merchant phenol: 18% steady-state EBITDA margin (FY23-26 group average ~14%; FY21-22 peak 24-29%).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~26% of revenue in FY29 to 5% (maintenance plus debottlenecking) by FY31, once PC/BPA are built.
dcf._yearsWhy: Two-stage DCF: explicit FY28-29 (peak capex), FY30 a transition year (half-way to steady state, with BPA/phenol-2 spend still running), steady state from FY31, then a terminal value at 6% growth. The engine fades capex in a straight line from the last forecast year; with the house 15-year horizon that keeps capex at 15-25% of revenue for a decade and the DCF turns negative. A short horizon is the only way to let capex fall back to maintenance levels once the project is finished.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Spreads stay firm as Chinese and European capacity closes and Haldia's new plant mostly replaces imports; AI margins return towards 18% as China curbs nitration and new products ramp; polycarbonate starts on time.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Phenol spreads fall back to the FY25-26 trough as Haldia's 345 ktpa plant and Chinese capacity flood the market; AI stays stuck near FY26 margins; polycarbonate slips again while debt and interest keep rising.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Deepak Nitrite: Motilal Oswal 24x and Prabhudas Lilladher 29x FY28E EPS (Aug-2026). 25x = the stock's ~36x one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 cut by the ~30% de-rating of Indian chemical stocks at 30-Sep-2026. Bull 32x (half the de-rating reverses), bear 20x (the 2020 level, before the phenol boom was priced in).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Charges the polycarbonate debt explicitly. 15x ≈ the ~23x five-year median EV/EBITDA less the same ~30% sector de-rating; peers at 30-Sep-2026: Aarti 16.0x, Vinati 16.9x, Atul 12.5x, SRF 19.8x trailing.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: explicit FY28-29, transition FY30, steady state FY31 (18% EBITDA margin, capex 5% of revenue), Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%, net debt deducted. It shows how much of the price depends on returns not yet visible.
